title: HiPhy: Hierarchical Alignment for Physically-Plausible Multi-Principle Video Generation
title_zh: HiPhy：面向物理合理多原理视频生成的分层对齐

paragraphs.en: Video generation models have achieved remarkable visual fidelity and have strong potential to become general-purpose world simulators. Despite this progress, they still fail to generate videos which adhere to laws of physics. The problem becomes even more apparent in realistic settings where multiple physical principles must work together within the same video; for example, ‘a balloon floating upward while steam rises from a pot’ requires buoyancy and fluid dynamics to unfold coherently and simultaneously. Yet existing methods largely ignore multi-principle interactions, focusing on a single principle per video. We propose HiPhy ( Hi erarchical Phy sical Alignment), a reinforcement learning framework that grounds video generation in physical laws through a dual-level objective: locally enforcing the temporal dynamics of individual physical principles, and globally ensuring the physical and semantic coherence of the entire scene. To support multi-principle generation, we construct a 50K-prompt dataset and introduce a prompt benchmark MultiPhyBench , spanning a diverse range of co-occurring physical events. Our experiments show that HiPhy significantly outperforms prior methods and baselines, improving physical commonsense and semantic alignment significantly across various benchmarks, with the largest gains on scenes involving multiple concurrent physical principles where competing methods degrade most sharply.

paragraphs.en: Video diffusion models [ 23 , 35 ] have made remarkable progress in producing high-resolution, temporally coherent videos [ 38 , 49 ] . This rapid progress has made video generation models promising candidates for general-purpose world simulators that are capable of synthesizing diverse physical scenarios on demand for embodied AI, robotics simulation, scientific visualization, and counterfactual reasoning [ 17 , 22 , 19 , 1 ] .
paragraphs.zh: 视频扩散模型 [ 23 , 35 ] 在生成高分辨率、时间上连贯的视频方面取得了显著进展 [ 38 , 49 ] 。 这一快速进展使视频生成模型成为通用世界模拟器的有力候选，能够按需合成多样的物理场景，服务于具身智能、机器人仿真、科学可视化和反事实推理 [ 17 , 22 , 19 , 1 ] 。

sents.en: Video diffusion models [ 23 , 35 ] have made remarkable progress in producing high-resolution, temporally coherent videos [ 38 , 49 ] .
sents.zh: 视频扩散模型 [ 23 , 35 ] 在生成高分辨率、时间上连贯的视频方面取得了显著进展 [ 38 , 49 ] 。

sents.en: This rapid progress has made video generation models promising candidates for general-purpose world simulators that are capable of synthesizing diverse physical scenarios on demand for embodied AI, robotics simulation, scientific visualization, and counterfactual reasoning [ 17 , 22 , 19 , 1 ] .
sents.zh: 这一快速进展使视频生成模型成为通用世界模拟器的有力候选，能够按需合成多样的物理场景，服务于具身智能、机器人仿真、科学可视化和反事实推理 [ 17 , 22 , 19 , 1 ] 。

paragraphs.en: Despite their visual fidelity, current video generators routinely produce clips that violate elementary physical laws, such as momentum, fluid dynamics, and material properties [ 22 , 17 ] . We argue this reflects a deeper representational gap: because models are trained merely to maximize frame likelihood given text [ 13 , 12 ] , they reproduce plausible patterns from their vast training data without reasoning about the underlying mechanisms [ 30 , 8 ] . Consider a prompt “an apple falls into water,” which entails two co-occurring physical principles: rigid-body and fluid dynamics (see Fig. 2 ). We find this representational gap manifests in two consistent failure modes on such compound prompts: (1) Principle Omission , where models ignore secondary physics, for instance, the apple drops realistically but the water remains undisturbed; and (2) Temporal Shortcutting , where unfolding dynamics are collapsed into a single visual snapshot, such as rendering the splash as a static spraying effect instead of progressing through impact → \rightarrow crown formation . Importantly, these failures do not reflect a deficit in visual capability; given sufficiently detailed text, modern video models generate individual physical principles with striking fidelity. The core challenge is finding a systematic mechanism to elicit this latent knowledge along two dimensions: the presence of each principle and its temporal structure. This motivates HiPhy ’s dual-level design: per-principle supervision targets Principle Omission , while fine-grained sub-stage reward design addresses Temporal Shortcutting .
paragraphs.zh: 尽管当前视频生成器具有很高的视觉保真度，但其生成的视频片段常常违反基本的物理定律，例如动量、流体动力学和材料属性 [22, 17]。 我们认为这反映了一个更深层的表示差距：由于模型仅仅以在给定文本的条件下最大化帧似然为目标进行训练 [13, 12]，它们只是从海量训练数据中复现看似合理的模式，而并未对背后的机制进行推理 [30, 8]。 以提示词“一个苹果落入水中”为例，它包含两个同时发生的物理原理：刚体动力学和流体动力学（见图 2）。 我们发现，在这类复合提示词上，这一表示差距表现为两种一致的失败模式：（1）原理遗漏，即模型忽略次要的物理原理，例如苹果下落得很逼真，但水面却毫无波动；（2）时间捷径，即将逐步展开的动力学过程压缩为单一的视觉快照，例如把水花渲染成静止的喷溅效果，而不是逐步呈现撞击 → \rightarrow 冠状水花形成的过程。 重要的是，这些失败并非源于视觉能力的不足；只要文本描述足够详细，现代视频模型就能以惊人的保真度生成单一物理原理的画面。 核心挑战在于找到一种系统性机制，从两个维度激发这种潜在知识：每个原理是否出现，以及它的时间结构。 这促成了 HiPhy 的双层设计：逐原理监督针对原理遗漏问题，而细粒度的子阶段奖励设计则解决时间捷径问题。

paragraphs.en: Existing efforts to inject physical knowledge into video models largely rely on 3D engines [ 27 , 29 , 6 ] , fine-tuning [ 5 , 41 , 11 , 40 ] , or inference-time guidance [ 48 , 14 , 45 , 25 , 33 , 16 ] . While 3D engines can simulate concurrent dynamics, they are computationally heavy and constrained to rigid domains. Conversely, learning-based and guidance methods offer flexibility but typically supervise only a single physical principle per video. Consequently, they lack mechanisms to ensure compound events are jointly satisfied. Empirically, we observe these latter methods degrade sharply as concurrent processes increase, often dropping one principle entirely.
paragraphs.zh: 现有将物理知识注入视频模型的工作主要依赖 3D 引擎 [27, 29, 6]、微调 [5, 41, 11, 40] 或推理时引导 [48, 14, 45, 25, 33, 16]。 虽然 3D 引擎能够模拟并发动态，但其计算开销大，且局限于刚性领域。 相反，基于学习和引导的方法较为灵活，但通常每段视频只监督单一物理原理。 因此，它们缺乏确保复合事件被共同满足的机制。 从经验上看，我们观察到这些后一类方法随着并发过程增多而急剧退化，往往完全丢失某一原理。

paragraphs.en: In this paper, we propose HiPhy ( Hi erarchical Phy sical Alignment), a reinforcement learning framework that closes the previously mentioned gap by formulating compound physical events as a hierarchical alignment problem. By optimizing each physical principle locally, HiPhy enables physically grounded video generation in concurrent, multi-principle scenes. Our key insight is that physical plausibility is fundamentally both a temporal and a compositional property. While modern video generators struggle to reason about the temporal progression of physical events, leading to Principle Omission and Temporal Shortcutting , we model multi-principle scenes as compositions of independent, temporally structured physical principles. Consequently, we introduce a novel training objective that explicitly enforces stage-level supervision across each concurrent physical principle. HiPhy mirrors this insight through a hierarchical alignment framework. At the foundational level, we explicitly optimize for the chronological progression of each physical event by breaking it into smaller stages. At the same time, we align these stages with global video coherence and semantic alignment objectives, ensuring that multi-principle interactions compose naturally while maintaining semantic and visual coherence. Crucially, when a prompt contains multiple concurrent physical events, HiPhy treats each as an independent learning stream, preventing high-variance signals from washing out the gradient. Our contributions are summarized as follows:

paragraphs.en: Physically Plausible Video Generation One line of work fine-tunes video backbones on large physically annotated datasets [ 5 , 41 , 11 , 40 ] . Because such models lack explicit physical knowledge, generation quality remains tightly coupled to training-set coverage and rarely transfers to the diversity of real-world scenarios [ 30 , 17 ] . A second line injects physical knowledge through 3D engines such as Blender or Unreal, depth or edge predictors, or auxiliary 3D objectives [ 27 , 29 , 21 ] , and graphics rendering pipelines [ 2 ] . These methods are precise but constrained to fixed physical categories and incur heavy computational cost, particularly for phenomena such as fluids or steam [ 6 ] . paragraphs.en: RL-based Video Generation Prior work adapts preference learning to video along several axes. VideoDPO [ 26 ] extends DPO to text-to-video diffusion with an omni-preference objective balancing visual quality and text relevance. Flow-DPO [ 24 ] aligns flow-matching video generators using a multi-dimensional reward, improving motion smoothness and prompt adherence over SFT and alternative RLHF variants. More fine-grained supervision has also been explored via DenseDPO [ 44 ] , which targets temporal locality by densifying video preferences across time. Complementary directions include GRPO variants tailored to video control, such as DanceGRPO [ 46 ] for learning temporally coherent policies. Additionally, methods such as [ 42 , 7 ] provide global supervision over state properties. Unlike these methods, HiPhy is the first to handle multi-principle physical scenes by integrating a hierarchical objective that targets per-principle optimization in its training.

paragraphs.en: Given a user prompt q q describing n n concurrent physical principles and a frozen text-to-video model 𝒢 \mathcal{G} , HiPhy learns a policy π θ \pi_{\theta} such that the video v = 𝒢 ⁡ ( p ) v=\mathcal{G}(p) generated from p ∼ π θ ( ⋅ ∣ q ) p\sim\pi_{\theta}(\cdot\mid q) depicts all n n principles with the correct temporal progression of their sub-stages. Two insights shape this design: (i) Modern video models already possess strong visual priors over individual physical phenomena but lack explicit temporal structure for how a physical event should unfold; surfacing this structure at the prompt level is therefore more sample-efficient than retraining the backbone, (ii) Generating complex physical scenes demands compositional reasoning; a video may generate one physical principle faithfully yet fail to compose multiple principles together. We train a reasoning policy π θ \pi_{\theta} via GRPO [ 32 ] using a hierarchical compositional objective. By explicitly isolating each concurrent physical principle and enforcing the temporal progression of its individual sub-stages, our policy guarantees the structural integrity of compound scenes.

paragraphs.en: We construct a 50K-prompt training dataset and introduce MultiPhyBench, a 1000-prompt evaluation suite in which each prompt describes up to three simultaneous physical events. To generate these, we extract single-principle processes and their domains from VideoPhy2 [ 4 ] and WISA-80k [ 39 ] , sample combinations of 1–3 events, and use an LLM [ 47 ] to filter out implausible co-occurrences. For each valid combination, we generate a unified video prompt and a chronologically ordered hierarchical tree for each constituent principle (Fig. 2 ). These hierarchical annotations serve as pseudo-labels for our local reward (Sec. 4.2 ). Full curation details are provided in the SM A .

paragraphs.en: We introduce HiPhy , a hierarchical physical alignment framework that scores the temporal progression of each physical principle in a fine-grained fashion (see Fig. 3 for an overview). Consider an input prompt p p describing n n physical principles { p ( i ) } i = 1 n \{p^{(i)}\}_{i=1}^{n} . During data curation, each physical principle p ( i ) p^{(i)} is paired with an ordered tree 𝒯 ∗ ( i ) \mathcal{T}^{*(i)} of depth D ( i ) D^{(i)} in which each node represents a stage within that physical principle. For “an apple falls into water and submerges,” the outer level nodes are falling → \rightarrow splash on contact → \rightarrow submerging . The stage splash on contact then further expands into impact → \rightarrow crown formation (Fig. 2 ). Nodes in each level are temporally ordered, meaning that the completion of one node depends on the completion of the nodes before it. During training, we generate a video, v ^ \hat{v} , using a backbone video diffusion model, 𝒢 \mathcal{G} noted as v ^ = 𝒢 ⁡ ( p ) \hat{v}=\mathcal{G}(p) . To evaluate how well the generated video, v ^ \hat{v} , depicts each physical principle { p ( i ) } i = 1 n \{p^{(i)}\}_{i=1}^{n} , we extract a similar hierarchical structure as 𝒯 ∗ ( i ) \mathcal{T}^{*(i)} from v ^ \hat{v} for each physical principle p ( i ) p^{(i)} . This procedure is done in the same way as detailed in SM Sec. A . Formally, given a VLM extractor, ℛ \mathcal{R} , we derive an observed tree, 𝒯 ^ ( i ) = ℛ ⁡ ( v ^ , p ( i ) ) \hat{\mathcal{T}}^{(i)}=\mathcal{R}(\hat{v},p^{(i)}) , that decomposes the observed stages in the generated video into a hierarchically ordered tree.

paragraphs.en: Global Video Reward. The local reward captures fine-grained temporal progression within each process but does not guarantee that the video is semantically faithful to the prompt, visually coherent, or consistent with broader physical commonsense. We introduce a global reward term R global R_{\text{global}} with three complementary terms. First, HPSv2 [ 43 ] captures visual quality and aesthetic alignment, averaged over T T uniformly sampled frames to obtain R HPS R_{\text{HPS}} . Second, a physics VLM judge 𝒥 \mathcal{J} (VideoPhy2 [ 4 ] ) rates physical commonsense R PC R_{\text{PC}} , assessing whether the primary action follows real-world physical rules, and semantic alignment R SA R_{\text{SA}} , measuring whether events described in q q actually appear in v ^ \hat{v} . All three terms are linearly normalized to [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] and combined into a single scalar:

paragraphs.en: Figure 4 illustrates the diverse physical principles our method handles compared to the Wan [ 38 ] backbone. Scenes span rigid-body dynamics ( bouncing ball, sliced apple, catching a baseball ), fluid-rigid interactions ( leaf falling into a puddle ), athletic motion ( somersault, skateboarding ), and concurrent multi-principle events ( smoke beside dripping honey , squeezing toothpaste ). In these scenarios, Wan frequently fails: balls bounce implausibly or multiply randomly, leaves disappear into water rather than floating, and athletic motions collapse. paragraphs.en: Figure 5 compares our method against Wan and three physics-aware baselines: inference-time optimization (Predict-and-Perturb [ 16 ] ), iterative LLM refinement (PhyT2V [ 45 ] ), and finetuning (WISA [ 39 ] ). The results reveal consistent baseline failure modes that compound as the physical event count increases. On two-principle prompts like “ book sliding while a ball falls ”, Fig. 5 , a , baselines struggle with coherent interaction: Wan and PnP omit the sliding book , PhyT2V hallucinates extra objects, and WISA produces static scenes. Similarly, in Fig. 5 , b , gradual integration is often skipped. This performance gap widens on three-principle prompts (bottom). Baselines routinely drop key elements, such as the simmering sauce or rain in Fig. 5 , c , or the boiling water and whisking action in Fig. 5 , d . In contrast, our method coherently generates all constituent processes without degrading overall video quality, which we attribute to optimizing each process as a separate local reward stream during training.

paragraphs.en: We evaluate our method across multiple physical benchmarks such as Videophy2 and PhyWorldBench [ 4 , 10 ] . We assess physical commonsense (PC) and semantic alignment (SA) using Gemini 3 Flash [ 36 ] , which supports higher frame rates. Additionally, we report a “PC & SA” metric that measures the fraction of videos that are simultaneously physically grounded and semantically aligned. To assess robustness beyond physics-specific benchmarks, we also compare against baselines on VBench [ 15 ] , summarizing its orthogonal dimensions into two axes: Dynamics (subject and background consistency, motion smoothness, dynamic degree) and Appearance (imaging and aesthetic quality). Table 1 reports results across two single-principle benchmarks (VideoPhy2 [ 4 ] and PhyWorldBench [ 10 ] ) and our curated multi-principle benchmark of 1K prompts containing concurrent physical principles. HiPhy achieves the strongest performance on all physics benchmarks. Our method significantly outperforms the best baselines on VideoPhy2 (+10% physical, +16% alignment) and PhyWorldBench ( ≈ \approx +30% physical, +45% semantic), demonstrating the strength of our hierarchical reward. While generating concurrent physical events remains challenging across all methods, our per-principle hierarchical optimization preserves distinct learning signals, maintaining the largest margin on the multi-principle benchmark. Finally, VBench [ 15 ] evaluations confirm that physics-aware training preserves general video quality. Both Dynamics and Appearance match or exceed the Wan2.1 baseline, as our global reward terms effectively anchor overall coherence.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在多个物理基准（如 Videophy2 和 PhyWorldBench [4, 10]）上评估我们的方法。 我们使用 Gemini 3 Flash [36] 评估物理常识（PC）和语义对齐（SA），该模型支持更高的帧率。 此外，我们报告一个“PC & SA”指标，用于衡量同时满足物理合理性和语义对齐的视频比例。 为了评估超越物理专用基准的鲁棒性，我们还在 VBench [15] 上与基线进行比较，并将其正交维度归纳为两个轴：动态（主体和背景一致性、运动平滑度、动态程度）和外观（成像与美学质量）。 表 1 报告了两个单原则基准（VideoPhy2 [4] 和 PhyWorldBench [10]）以及我们精选的包含并发物理原则的 1K 提示多原则基准上的结果。 HiPhy 在所有物理基准上取得了最强的性能。 我们的方法在 VideoPhy2（物理 +10%，对齐 +16%）和 PhyWorldBench（物理约 +30%，语义 +45%）上显著优于最佳基线，展示了我们分层奖励的优势。 尽管对所有方法而言，生成并发物理事件仍然具有挑战性，但我们针对每个原则的分层优化保留了各自独立的学习信号，在多原则基准上保持了最大的领先幅度。 最后，VBench [15] 的评估证实，物理感知训练能够保持通用的视频质量。 动态和外观均达到或超过 Wan2.1 基线，因为我们的全局奖励项有效地锚定了整体一致性。

paragraphs.en: We compare the inference time of our method against prior physics-grounded video generation baselines on a single H200 GPU. paragraphs.en: Figure 7 (A–C) illustrates performance as the number of concurrent principles per prompt increases. While all methods degrade with rising complexity, baselines exhibit a sharp collapse; PnP and PhyT2V lose approximately half their PC scores between 1- and 3-process prompts, with joint PC & SA scores falling below 20. In contrast, HiPhy maintains a joint score of approximately 50, widening the performance gap as complexity grows. paragraphs.zh: 图 7（A–C）展示了随着每个提示中并发原则数量增加时的性能表现。 尽管所有方法都随复杂度上升而性能下降，但基线方法出现了急剧崩溃；从 1 过程提示到 3 过程提示，PnP 和 PhyT2V 的 PC 分数损失约一半，其 PC 与 SA 的联合分数降至 20 以下。 相比之下，HiPhy 保持了约 50 的联合分数，并且随着复杂度增长，性能差距不断扩大。 我们将这种鲁棒性归因于我们的逐过程奖励流，它为每个事件提供独立的学习信号。 这避免了基线方法中出现的梯度稀释问题，那些方法试图将多过程的正确性压缩为单一标量。

paragraphs.en: We presented a reinforcement learning approach to physics-grounded video generation that decomposes physical correctness into per-principle local rewards over temporal sub-stages and a global reward for semantic and visual coherence. Across VideoPhy2, PhyWorldBench, and our multi-principle benchmark, HiPhy achieves the strongest physical commonsense and semantic alignment, with the largest margins on prompts containing multiple concurrent principles, where prior methods degrade most sharply. These results suggest that explicit temporal decomposition, combined with a learned refinement signal, is an effective approach to closing the gap between video generation and physical realism.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了一种基于强化学习的物理接地视频生成方法，将物理正确性分解为时间子阶段上的逐原则局部奖励，以及用于语义与视觉一致性的全局奖励。 在VideoPhy2、PhyWorldBench以及我们的多原则基准上，HiPhy实现了最强的物理常识与语义对齐，在包含多个并发原则的提示上优势最大，而先前方法在此类提示上的性能下降最为显著。 这些结果表明，显式的时间分解结合学习到的细化信号，是弥合视频生成与物理真实性之间差距的有效方法。

paragraphs.en: Existing physical video datasets and benchmarks evaluate physical plausibility along a single process per prompt (e.g., a ball rolling down an incline or water pouring into a glass). However, real-world scenes routinely involve multiple physical processes unfolding simultaneously. To model physical realism in multi-process settings, we construct a dataset in which each prompt describes multiple concurrent physical events. The number of processes per prompt, n n , scales with the video length; for instance, at 81 frames we support up to three simultaneous processes.
paragraphs.zh: 现有的物理视频数据集和基准测试在每条提示（prompt）下仅沿单一物理过程评估物理合理性（例如，球沿斜面滚下，或水倒入玻璃杯）。 然而，现实世界的场景中通常会同时展开多个物理过程。 为了在多过程设置中建模物理真实性，我们构建了一个数据集，其中每条提示描述多个同时发生的物理事件。 每条提示的过程数量 n n 随视频长度而扩展；例如，在 81 帧时我们支持最多三个同时进行的过程。

paragraphs.en: We collect single-process physical concepts from existing datasets, including VideoPhy2 [ 4 ] and WISA-80k [ 39 ] . For each source prompt, we use a large language model to extract the underlying physical process along with its physics domain. For instance, from the prompt “a bowling ball rolls off a table and hits the ground,” we extract the process “ball rolling and falling” with the domain rigid-body dynamics ; from “steam rises from a boiling pot,” we extract “water boiling” with the domain thermodynamics .
paragraphs.zh: 我们从现有数据集中收集单过程物理概念，包括 VideoPhy2 [4] 和 WISA-80k [39]。 对于每个源提示词，我们使用大语言模型提取其背后的物理过程及其所属的物理领域。 例如，从提示词“一个保龄球从桌上滚落并砸到地面”中，我们提取出过程“球的滚动与下落”，其领域为刚体动力学；从“蒸汽从沸腾的锅中升起”中，我们提取出“水沸腾”，其领域为热力学。

paragraphs.en: We sample subsets of 1, 2, or 3 physical concepts per prompt. paragraphs.en: To validate that the sub-stages extracted by our pipeline correspond to events that humans actually perceive in the underlying videos, we conducted a small-scale human study on 50 randomly sampled videos spanning six physics domains. Each video was rated by 5 annotators on a 1–5 Likert scale along two axes: how clearly each sub-stage was depicted and whether the sub-stages occurred in the listed chronological order. Table 4 reports the results. The mean stage-quality rating of 4.21/5 and ordering rating of 4.42/5 indicate that our extracted decompositions are faithful to the videos at both the level of individual sub-stages and their temporal arrangement. Scores are consistent across domains, with optics events scoring lowest (3.88), reflecting the difficulty of extracting discrete temporal stages from scenes dominated by events such as reflection and scattering. Furthermore, We conduct a human evaluation survey on whether extracted stages are physically valid. Each of the 50 videos was rated by all 5 raters, giving 250 individual ratings, and the resulting estimates are precise with mean pairwise percent agreement of 0.853 0.853 , with inter-rater agreement of 0.861 0.861 using Gwet’s AC2.
paragraphs.zh: 为了验证我们的流程提取出的子阶段确实对应于人类在底层视频中实际感知到的事件，我们在50个随机采样的视频上开展了一项小规模人类研究，这些视频涵盖六个物理学领域。 每个视频由5名标注者按照1–5的Likert量表在两个维度上进行评分：各子阶段被呈现得是否清晰，以及子阶段是否按照所列出的时间顺序发生。 表4报告了结果。 阶段质量的平均评分为4.21/5，顺序的平均评分为4.42/5，这表明我们提取的分解在单个子阶段层面及其时间排列层面都与视频内容相符。 各领域的评分保持一致，其中光学事件的得分最低（3.88），这反映出从以反射和散射等事件为主导的场景中提取离散时间阶段的难度。 此外，我们针对提取的阶段在物理上是否有效开展了一项人类评估调查。 这50个视频中的每一个都由全部5名评分者进行评分，共得到250条个人评分，所得的估计结果十分精确，评分者两两一致百分比的平均值为0.853 0.853，使用Gwet的AC2计算的评分者间一致性为0.861 0.861。

paragraphs.en: Additionally, to validate physical structure, 10 physics graduate raters evaluated decompositions for 20 canonical events, with 10 corrupted trees interspersed and unmarked; 5 with stages shuffled out of chronological order, 5 with a physically impossible stage inserted. Raters were told only that some decompositions contained errors. Table 5 shows the average score collected from these 10 raters. As seen, the extracted trees score comparably and the corrupted variants scores are low, with the largest gap on ordering, where shuffling the stages is the most direct violation of physical sequence. This confirms that raters were evaluating physical validity, and that our reference decompositions reflect the physical structure of each event.

paragraphs.en: We remove the sub-stages from each reference tree, keeping only the top-level stages. This gives a flat reward and is the depth-one special case of our formulation. The flat reward barely hurts VideoPhy2, where each prompt has one physical principle, but degrades MultiPhyBench sharply. The reason is that a top-level stage such as "splash" is satisfied by any splash at all. Without sub-stages the reward cannot separate a static spray from a real impact followed by crown formation, so it stops pushing the model once each principle is roughly present. This matters most when several principles must unfold at once.
paragraphs.zh: 我们从每棵参考树中移除子阶段，只保留顶层阶段。 这给出一个扁平奖励，也是我们 formulations 的深度为 1 的特例。 扁平奖励对 VideoPhy2 几乎没有损害，因为每个提示只涉及一个物理原理，但在 MultiPhyBench 上性能急剧下降。 原因在于，像「splash」这样的顶层阶段只要出现任何溅水就能被满足。 没有子阶段，奖励就无法区分静止的喷雾和真正撞击后形成的冠状水花，因此一旦每个原理大致出现，它就不再推动模型改进。 当多个原理必须同时展开时，这一点最为关键。

paragraphs.en: Each stream is standardized against its own mean and standard deviation over the group, so every principle contributes comparably to the advantage. Without it, a stream that varies more widely dominates and the policy maximizes that one term while ignoring the rest, degrading alignment and multi-process scenes (second row). The 1 n \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} rescaling addresses a different problem. Summing more terms inflates the variance of the advantage, so a three-principle sample pushes the gradient harder than a one-principle sample; the rescaling holds this variance constant. It also preserves the balance between the two reward families, since the advantage combines one global stream with a sum of n local ones. Without the factor the local sum overwhelms the global term and the policy loses the signal anchoring generation to prompt semantics and visual coherence, visible as the SA drop in the third row. At N = 1 N=1 the factor is inactive and per-stream normalization has little to balance, with only one local stream alongside the global one; the differences emerge as principles co-occur.
paragraphs.zh: 每条流都在组内按其自身的均值和标准差进行标准化，因此每个原则对优势的贡献具有可比性。 若没有这一步，波动幅度更大的流会占据主导，策略会最大化那一项而忽略其余各项，从而损害对齐效果和多进程场景（第二行）。 1 n \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} 的缩放解决的是另一个问题。 累加更多的项会放大优势的方差，因此包含三个原则的样本会比只含一个原则的样本对梯度的推动更强；该缩放使这一方差保持恒定。 它还保持了两个奖励族之间的平衡，因为优势将一条全局流与 n 条局部流之和结合在一起。 若没有该因子，局部之和会压过全局项，策略会失去将生成锚定于提示语义和视觉一致性的信号，表现为第三行中 SA 的下降。 在 N = 1 N=1 时该因子不起作用，且由于只有一条局部流与全局流并存，逐流标准化几乎没有需要平衡的对象；差异会随着原则的共同出现而显现出来。

paragraphs.en: To complement the automatic evaluations, we analyze survey results for videos containing multiple concurrent physical principles. We report the average ratings from 50 participants who evaluated the depiction of each physical event; a representative question from this study is shown in Fig. 8 . The user study included 30 distinct prompts across 5 different methods. As illustrated in Fig. 7 , A–C, our method consistently achieves the highest scores across all principles. Notably, while baseline performance is often unstable, dropping specific principles entirely within a scene or the inability to generate all of them plausibly, our approach maintains balanced adherence across the board. This validates our per-process reward design, which successfully allocates a distinct learning signal to each physical event.
paragraphs.zh: 为了补充自动评估，我们分析了包含多个并发物理原理的视频的调查结果。 我们报告了50名参与者对每个物理事件描绘情况进行评分的平均分；该研究的一个代表性问题如图8所示。 该用户研究涵盖5种不同方法的30个不同提示。 如图7 A–C所示，我们的方法在所有原理上均持续取得最高分数。 值得注意的是，基线的表现往往不稳定，例如场景中的某些原理完全丢失或无法合理地生成所有原理，而我们的方法在整体上保持均衡的符合度。 这验证了我们的逐过程奖励设计，该设计成功地为每个物理事件分配了独特的学习信号。
